transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-11
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Apex Lead ML Eng), Carlos Ruiz (Apex SRE), Lena Park (Apex Product)

Auto-summary: weekly POC sync focused on throughput / batching / concurrency; action items assigned for stress test and config/pricing follow-up.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan Lee): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see the Apex team. Quick agenda — Priya will run through the perf results from last week's run, then we want to dial in concurrency/batching knobs and agree on the next stress test and run the Dedicated pilot pricing discussion at the end.

00:24 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): Cool, I'll share my screen in a sec, but quick recap — we ran three profiles across the weekend: baseline (hosted, concurrency 16), medium (concurrency 40), and high (concurrency 80) with continuous batching enabled and prefix KV cache warmed. The baseline had stable p50 around 120ms but throughput plateaued at ~350 reqs/sec. Medium bumped to ~820 reqs/sec with p50 ~150ms, p95 420ms. High hit a peak of 1.6k reqs/sec but saw p95 tails jump to ~1.2s and some queue drops at the ingress.

01:02 Speaker 3 (Maya Chen): Sorry to jump in — when you say queue drops, is that at Redwood's request queue or our upstream LB? We saw some 503s in our app logs last night.

01:12 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): Good question. We correlated logs — most of the 503s were from the request queue timing out at Redwood's side because the server-side queue length hit the configured max_wait_ms and requests were evicted to avoid overloading the GPU. We can change the queue policy to prefer queuing over immediate rejection up to a point, but that will increase tail latency.

01:35 Speaker 4 (Carlos Ruiz): Right, we definitely want throughput but not the 1s+ tails. Our SLOs are p95 < 500ms end-to-end. Any suggestions to keep throughput while trimming tails?

01:47 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): A few levers — (1) increase concurrency but reduce per-request max tokens or split long requests server-side, (2) tune continuous batching slice size so very large batches are avoided, (3) warm KV cache more aggressively so cache misses don't spike latency, (4) implement a small front-end token-limited queuing layer to shed or down-prioritize heavy requests. For this POC I recommend keeping concurrency around 60 and adjusting batch max to 64 tokens per slice; that historically hits the sweet spot for this model family on the GPU type you're on.

02:18 Speaker 5 (Lena Park): When you say model family, are we on the same model variant across tests? I thought we had a quantized variant we were trying.

02:25 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): Good catch. We ran the tests on the standard fp16 variant. We did one short run using the 4-bit quantized variant — it reduced median latency by ~10-15% and increased steady-state throughput about 20%, but we saw slightly worse coherence for a small subset of prompts. So there is a trade-off: quantization helps throughput/cost, but we flagged a small quality regression on the eval set you provided.

02:52 Speaker 3 (Maya Chen): Quality regressions are sensitive for our billing descriptors use-case; we can't risk hallucinated amounts. Can you show the eval diffs?

03:02 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): Yep, I have the eval scoreboard in the deck — short summary: 98.7% exact-match on baseline, 97.9% on quantized for the critical fields. We can do targeted hybrid routing where high-risk prompts go to fp16 and lower-risk to quantized. That keeps unit cost down while preserving quality for sensitive flows.

03:28 Speaker 1 (Jordan Lee): That hybrid pattern is what many customers pick for production. For throughput targets, what's the recommended steady-state concurrency if we want to hit ~1k reqs/sec while keeping p95 under 500ms?

03:41 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): Based on the weekend runs and queuing model, target concurrency ~60 with continuous batching enabled and batch size cap set to 64 tokens, plus increasing server-side queue depth to 200 with a longer max_wait_ms. That should hit around 900–1,050 rps with p95 ~380–480ms after KV warm-up. If you want to push to 1.6k rps you'll need to either go to Dedicated capacity or lower quality via quantized variant and accept longer tails.

04:08 Speaker 4 (Carlos Ruiz): Dedicated is interesting — do you have numbers for reserved pools? We need predictable throughput for peak windows.

04:16 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): Yes, on Dedicated we can reserve a GPU pool and pin model replicas; that removes the public queue contention and gives more predictable p95s. For your traffic pattern (burst every hour, 10 min windows), a Dedicated pilot with auto-burst headroom gets you stable 1.4–1.6k rps with p95 ~350–450ms depending on model variant. Jordan will share pilot pricing.

04:42 Speaker 5 (Lena Park): Back to tuning — what about batching behavior for mixed request lengths? We have some short prompts and some long ones. Is there adaptive slicing?

04:53 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): Redwood uses continuous batching with dynamic slice thresholds. We observed that long-tail long requests can drag the batch. Two mitigations: set request size buckets (short vs long) and route to different queues, or enable slice_max_tokens so large requests are split across slices and don't hold up the batch. For your mixed profile, we'd recommend 2 queues: short queue optimized for <64 tokens, long queue for >64 tokens with slice_max_tokens 64.

05:22 Speaker 3 (Maya Chen): OK, can we see the dashboard queries you used? We want to replicate them in our Grafana.

05:29 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): I'll export the perf dashboard. It includes p50/p95/p99, request size distribution, batch size distribution, queue_wait_histogram, and GPU util. I'll share a link after the call.

05:40 Speaker 1 (Jordan Lee): Quick note on error handling — if you do the front-end shedding, Redwood's SDK has a built-in retry/backoff that understands queue rejections and will do jittered retries to reduce thundering herd. Just make sure retry budget is low so you don't amplify load.

06:01 Speaker 4 (Carlos Ruiz): In last night's test the retry logic cause a small spike — we need to tune that. We'll set retry budget to 2 and exponential backoff up to 200ms.

06:12 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): Great. Also want to call out KV cache warm-up: the weekend baselines warmed cache for 30 minutes before the run. If you start cold, first 10k tokens had 3–4x latency. For production you should use a warm-up pass or priority warm cache for heavy flows.

06:33 Speaker 5 (Lena Park): Are there any config flags to reduce tail jitter on the GPU side? We saw occasional 200ms spikes at p99.

06:40 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): A few: enable preemption-safe kernel scheduling, pin thread pools to cores to avoid jitter, and use the newer kernel selector profile that prefers lower-latency kernels at the cost of a little throughput. We can flip that for latency-sensitive routes.

07:03 Speaker 3 (Maya Chen): For the upcoming stress run you suggested concurrency 80 but earlier you said target 60. Which should we run?

07:12 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): Run both: a 2-hour sustained run at concurrency 60 to verify steady-state and a shorter 30–60 minute burst at 80 to expose tail behavior. That will help quantify if Dedicated or model ops are needed.

07:27 Speaker 1 (Jordan Lee): We'll put that in the action items. Also Jordan here — I'll send the Dedicated pilot pricing and the config worksheet with exact flags we used, plus the dashboard link.

07:39 Speaker 4 (Carlos Ruiz): One more ops question — what observability retention do you provide for per-request traces? We might need longer than default.

07:47 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): By default we store 30 days; we have enterprise retention add-on up to 365 days. For the pilot we can temporarily extend to 90 days to capture enough runs.

08:02 Speaker 5 (Lena Park): Any legal or data concerns for traces? We need PII scrubbed before shared with Redwood engineers.

08:09 Speaker 1 (Jordan Lee): Totally understood. We'll accept scrubbed traces or a hashed/obfuscated replay. For investigation the SE team only needs request metadata and token-level timings, not raw PII.

08:24 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): Ok quick recap of recommended config: continuous batching on, concurrency 60 steady-state, concurrency 80 short bursts, batch slice cap 64 tokens, server queue depth 200 with longer max_wait_ms, KV warm-up pass, and optional quantized variant for lower-cost routes with hybrid routing for safety-critical prompts.

08:50 Speaker 3 (Maya Chen): Sounds good. We'll run the 2h test starting Friday morning PT and share traces. Carlos will export the replay.

08:58 Speaker 4 (Carlos Ruiz): Yep, I'll get the traces and also tweak our client-side retry budget to 2.

09:05 Speaker 1 (Jordan Lee): Next steps again: Priya runs the stress test and shares logs, Jordan sends pricing and config worksheet, Carlos shares traces. Follow-up tentative on 2025-06-16 for results review. Any other blockers?

09:21 Speaker 5 (Lena Park): No blockers from product. Thanks everyone.

09:25 Speaker 2 (Priya Kapoor): I'll upload the dashboard queries and the eval diffs for the quantized variant. Expect links in chat.

09:32 Speaker 1 (Jordan Lee): Great, thanks all. We'll close early to respect time.

[end transcript]
